hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, east of Mozambique || narrow coastal plain, high plateau and mountains in center || world's fourth-largest island; strategic location along Mozambique Channel; despite Madagascar’s close proximity to the African continent, ocean currents isolate the island, resulting in high rates of endemic plant and animal species; approximately 90% of the flora and fauna on the island are found nowhere else || Resources: graphite, chromite, coal, bauxite, rare earth elements, salt, quartz, tar sands, semiprecious stones, mica, fish, hydropower || Exports: garments, nickel, vanilla, cloves, gold (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: narrow coastal plain, high plateau and mountains in center || Southern Africa, island in the Indian Ocean, east of Mozambique

climate.excerpt: tropical along coast, temperate inland, arid in south || periodic cyclones; drought; and locust infestation volcanism: Madagascar's volcanoes have not erupted in recorded history

economy.excerpt: low-income East African island economy; natural resource rich; extreme poverty; return of political stability has helped growth; sharp tax revenue drop due to COVID-19; leading vanilla producer; environmentally fragile || Exports: garments, nickel, vanilla, cloves, gold (2023) || Industries: meat processing, seafood, soap, beer, leather, sugar, textiles, glassware, cement, automobile assembly plant, paper, petroleum, tourism, mining

peopleAndCulture.excerpt: Malagasy (official) 99.9%, French (official) 23.6%, English 8.2%, other 0.6% (2018 est.) || Church of Jesus Christ in Madagascar/Malagasy Lutheran Church/Anglican Church 34%, Roman Catholic 32.3%, other Christian 8.1%, traditional/Animist 1.7%, Muslim 1.4%, other 0.6%, none 21.9% (2021 est.) || Malayo-Indonesian (Merina and related Betsileo), Cotiers (mixed African, Malayo-Indonesian, and Arab ancestry - Betsimisaraka, Tsimihety, Antaisaka, Sakalava), French, Indian, Creole, Comoran
